question: Assess the claim that Michael Jordan's scoring in 1990-91 was stronger than LeBron James's scoring in 2014-15. Compare regular-season and playoff scoring volume and shooting efficiency relative to the league. Compare teammates: core helpers first, then rotation scoring, minutes and recorded games. Check whether the per-game helper leaders adequately represent the supporting cast's recorded availability. Keep original samples and qualify any limited context.
response:
# Scoring Claim Review

**Verdict: Conditional: the broad claim is not uniformly supported across the selected metrics.**

> Michael Jordan's scoring in 1990-91 was stronger than LeBron James's scoring in 2014-15, comparing regular-season and playoff scoring volume, shooting efficiency, and supporting cast metrics.

This adjudication concerns the selected scoring statistics. It does not rank overall players or establish innate ability, defensive impact, or championship causation.

## Comparison contract

- Subjects: **Michael Jordan** and **LeBron James**.
- Scope: 1990-91–1990-91 versus 2014-15–2014-15; Regular Season, Playoffs.
- Statistical lens: overall scoring.
- Completed-season cutoff: **2025-26**; ongoing seasons are excluded.
- Percentages are recomputed from summed inputs. Missing observations remain missing.
- Relative efficiency uses same-season, same-phase league TS; career aggregation weights each season by FGA + 0.44 × FTA.

## Evidence selected by the Writer

- Regular Season / Accumulated points: Michael Jordan has the larger observed value. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- Regular Season / Points per game: Michael Jordan has the larger observed value. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- Playoffs / Accumulated points: LeBron James has the larger observed value. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

- Regular Season: accumulation versus scoring rate does not change the observed direction in this sample. Agreement on these metrics is not proof of overall superiority. - Regular Season: raw versus contemporaneous relative efficiency does not change the observed direction in this sample. Agreement on these metrics is not proof of overall superiority. - Playoffs: accumulation versus scoring rate changes the observed advantage. The broad claim therefore depends on this choice of lens. ## Core helpers and rotation context

The same anchor rule is used for both subjects: earliest and latest verified Finals in the approved window, otherwise recorded playoff endpoints. These are case studies, not complete-career teammate rankings.

| Michael Jordan / 1990-91 / Playoffs | Horace Grant | 13.29 | 39.18 | 17 | 61.95 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=270&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / 2014-15 / Playoffs | Kyrie Irving | 19 | 35.71 | 13 | 57.35 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |
| LeBron James / 2014-15 / Playoffs | Kevin Love | 14.25 | 26.71 | 4 | 57.74 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |

Core candidates are selected by contemporary scoring production, not by career reputation or an overall ability score. The main rotation is retained by total minutes; its full minutes, production and availability rows appear in the supporting-cast details below the report. Games played do not identify injuries or actual shared court time.

### Evidence-driven supporting-cast checks

The Lead checked whether the retrieved helper samples answer the question, in addition to checking whether the collectors ran. A candidate with fewer than half the maximum recorded games in the returned rotation triggers a sample-adequacy check; this is a declared screening rule, not a teammate ranking or exclusion threshold.

- **Addressed**: The per-game core list includes Kevin Love with sparse recorded appearances relative to the returned rotation. A matched regular-season baseline is needed before treating this playoff sample as typical supporting-cast context. Matched scoped evidence addresses the sample-adequacy question. Original observations remain visible; the additional phase does not replace them. | Michael Jordan | 1990-91 | Los Angeles Lakers | 4–1 | 31.2 | 61.17 | 70.7 | [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) |

Opponent regular-season record is one limited proxy. Finals wins and defeats are included; Finals-only player data must not be described as the whole postseason.

- Era-relative TS is a descriptive benchmark, not a causal correction for rules, physicality, spacing or defensive difficulty.
- True shooting uses the conventional 0.44 free-throw coefficient. It estimates shooting opportunities rather than counting actual possessions.
- Supporting-cast cases and opponent records are contextual samples. No teammate-swap or championship-credit calculation is justified.
- Linked evidence records retain exact scope, formulas, season inputs, original API parameters and retrieval timestamps. Aggregate citations use multiple API inputs; inspect the full source set in the evidence panel.
